{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Starting `fa` rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently drops the user's `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` (and `waiting`/`power.hold`/`auto_update`) sections.

**Root cause** (three cooperating defects):

1. `bin/fah_runapp.dart` `persistConfig` (~1553-1625) builds a **new** `CliConfig(...)` carrying only ~24 of the ~40 parsed fields. It never passes `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `contextWindowCap`/`stuckTool`/`agentLoadMode`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`, `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`tuiClassic`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `powerHold`, `skillsLiveRediscovery`, `links`, `compaction*`, `streamThinking`, `autoUpdate` — so those fields reset to constructor defaults in the object being saved.
2. `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~901-934) — the copy helper `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write step uses — drifted the same way: it also drops `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `agentMode`, `misuseBreaker`, `streamThinking`. Even a correct caller would lose those through the merge.
3. The disk-preservation backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (`cli_config.dart` ~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, so sections dropped by (1)/(2) are not re-attached from disk either. Additionally `CliConfig.toYaml()` never renders `spills:` (SpillsConfig has no renderer), and `persistConfig()` is invoked unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so every launch performs the lossy rewrite even when nothing changed.

**Impact**: any `fa` boot (or `/model`, `/provider`, mode/approval/tools/skills change — every `persistConfig` caller) permanently deletes the listed user sections from the global config. First reported on 1.0.547, verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d.

**Fix approach**:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`: add a complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); reimplement `withCustomProviders` as `copyWith(customProviders: entries)` so the copy helper can never drift again; render `spills:` in `toYaml()` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and render `agent.misuseBreaker: false` so the raw `agent:` block carries every parsed key; extend `_diskPreservedSections` with `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`; skip the temp-file+rename in `saveCliConfig` when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text (no write at boot when nothing changed).
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every parsed field rides along from `saved` by construction, so the save can no longer drop a section; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (per-folder model state) unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Starting `fa` rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently drops the user's `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` (and `waiting`/`power.hold`/`auto_update`) sections.

**Root cause** (three cooperating defects):

1. `bin/fah_runapp.dart` `persistConfig` (~1553-1625) builds a **new** `CliConfig(...)` carrying only ~24 of the ~40 parsed fields. It never passes `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `contextWindowCap`/`stuckTool`/`agentLoadMode`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`, `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`tuiClassic`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `powerHold`, `skillsLiveRediscovery`, `links`, `compaction*`, `streamThinking`, `autoUpdate` — so those fields reset to constructor defaults in the object being saved.
2. `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~901-934) — the copy helper `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write step uses — drifted the same way: it also drops `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `agentMode`, `misuseBreaker`, `streamThinking`. Even a correct caller would lose those through the merge.
3. The disk-preservation backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (`cli_config.dart` ~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, so sections dropped by (1)/(2) are not re-attached from disk either. Additionally `CliConfig.toYaml()` never renders `spills:` (SpillsConfig has no renderer), and `persistConfig()` is invoked unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so every launch performs the lossy rewrite even when nothing changed.

**Impact**: any `fa` boot (or `/model`, `/provider`, mode/approval/tools/skills change — every `persistConfig` caller) permanently deletes the listed user sections from the global config. First reported on 1.0.547, verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d.

**Fix approach**:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`: add a complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); reimplement `withCustomProviders` as `copyWith(customProviders: entries)` so the copy helper can never drift again; render `spills:` in `toYaml()` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and render `agent.misuseBreaker: false` so the raw `agent:` block carries every parsed key; extend `_diskPreservedSections` with `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`; skip the temp-file+rename in `saveCliConfig` when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text (no write at boot when nothing changed).
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every parsed field rides along from `saved` by construction, so the save can no longer drop a section; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (per-folder model state) unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Starting `fa` rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently drops the user's `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` (and `waiting`/`power.hold`/`auto_update`) sections.

**Root cause** (three cooperating defects):

1. `bin/fah_runapp.dart` `persistConfig` (~1553-1625) builds a **new** `CliConfig(...)` carrying only ~24 of the ~40 parsed fields. It never passes `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `contextWindowCap`/`stuckTool`/`agentLoadMode`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`, `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`tuiClassic`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `powerHold`, `skillsLiveRediscovery`, `links`, `compaction*`, `streamThinking`, `autoUpdate` — so those fields reset to constructor defaults in the object being saved.
2. `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~901-934) — the copy helper `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write step uses — drifted the same way: it also drops `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `agentMode`, `misuseBreaker`, `streamThinking`. Even a correct caller would lose those through the merge.
3. The disk-preservation backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (`cli_config.dart` ~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, so sections dropped by (1)/(2) are not re-attached from disk either. Additionally `CliConfig.toYaml()` never renders `spills:` (SpillsConfig has no renderer), and `persistConfig()` is invoked unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so every launch performs the lossy rewrite even when nothing changed.

**Impact**: any `fa` boot (or `/model`, `/provider`, mode/approval/tools/skills change — every `persistConfig` caller) permanently deletes the listed user sections from the global config. First reported on 1.0.547, verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d.

**Fix approach**:

**Bug**: Starting `fa` rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently drops the user's `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` (and `waiting`/`power.hold`/`auto_update`) sections.

**Root cause** (three cooperating defects):

1. `bin/fah_runapp.dart` `persistConfig` (~1553-1625) builds a **new** `CliConfig(...)` carrying only ~24 of the ~40 parsed fields. It never passes `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `contextWindowCap`/`stuckTool`/`agentLoadMode`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`, `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`tuiClassic`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `powerHold`, `skillsLiveRediscovery`, `links`, `compaction*`, `streamThinking`, `autoUpdate` — so those fields reset to constructor defaults in the object being saved.
2. `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~901-934) — the copy helper `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write step uses — drifted the same way: it also drops `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `agentMode`, `misuseBreaker`, `streamThinking`. Even a correct caller would lose those through the merge.
3. The disk-preservation backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (`cli_config.dart` ~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, so sections dropped by (1)/(2) are not re-attached from disk either. Additionally `CliConfig.toYaml()` never renders `spills:` (SpillsConfig has no renderer), and `persistConfig()` is invoked unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so every launch performs the lossy rewrite even when nothing changed.

**Impact**: any `fa` boot (or `/model`, `/provider`, mode/approval/tools/skills change — every `persistConfig` caller) permanently deletes the listed user sections from the global config. First reported on 1.0.547, verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d.

**Fix approach**:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`: add a complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); reimplement `withCustomProviders` as `copyWith(customProviders: entries)` so the copy helper can never drift again; render `spills:` in `toYaml()` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and render `agent.misuseBreaker: false` so the raw `agent:` block carries every parsed key; extend `_diskPreservedSections` with `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`; skip the temp-file+rename in `saveCliConfig` when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text (no write at boot when nothing changed).
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every parsed field rides along from `saved` by construction, so the save can no longer drop a section; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (per-folder model state) unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix).
"}

The `compaction:` section is fully-typed and STRICT: only `engine` (classic|structured) and `judgeBudgetSeconds` parse — anything else throws at load. So a raw compaction block has exactly the two keys; the typed render is value-faithful. The only fidelity loss is intra-block comments.

Given the strictness, carrying saved.compaction is value-identical always. But the documented promise ("the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead") would become slightly untrue (comments).

Decision: honor the documented design EXACTLY — persistConfig must not carry compaction. To enable that cleanly with copyFrom-style semantics, I'll keep copyWith uniform BUT... hmm.

Actually — cleanest minimal solution: keep my copyWith null=keep AND simply have bin NOT pass the two `compactionEngine: null, compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds: null` args (they're no-ops), while making the copyWith base for compaction NOT saved... no.

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. What if the copyWith call passes overlays, and afterwards we let the BACKSTOP do its documented job for compaction by REMOVING the carried compaction from the emitted yaml? That's emitter logic, not caller logic — wrong layer.

Alternative: `_diskPreservedSections` re-attach only fires when omitted. What if `compaction` render... no, don't hack the emitter.

Let me reconsider: sentinel-clearing for ALL nullable section fields? That's the "proper" copyWith in many codebases: use a per-field sentinel wrapper. Too invasive.

PRAGMATIC FINAL DECISION: Give `copyWith` two extra OPTIONAL clearing parameters? No.

Honestly — re-examine the actual risk of carrying saved.compaction once more:
1. Settings-hub session scope: sets liveCompactionEngine; persistConfig NOT called by that flow (nothing else triggers) → no write → promise holds. Even if a later unrelated persistConfig happens in the same session: we persist saved.compaction (the global value loaded at boot) — NOT the session pick. No leak. ✓
2. Global scope: `_upsertConfigYaml(['compaction','engine'], ...)` writes the yaml surgically; liveCompactionEngine set. persistConfig never carries the LIVE value (it reads saved.*, loaded pre-session). Next boot loads the upserted file. ✓
3. Intra-block comments: lost on the next whole-file save that changes something. Minor, consistent with... hmm, actually NOT consistent: other raw-preserved blocks with NO renderer (memory, a2a, waiting) keep comments forever. Blocks WITH renders that are carried (redact, images, links, tools, cube, tui, trajectory, quota, agent...) lose intra-block comments on any content-changing save. compaction was the exception BECAUSE the flow deliberately avoided persisting it.

The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). With the leak concern gone, the remaining difference is only intra-block comment fidelity — and the emitter renders compaction only when non-default values exist.

Hmm, but wait — one more scenario to check: `boot resolved` value! Let me check how boot resolves the engine: is there a `--compaction` flag or project override that lands in `saved`? `saved = loadCliConfig(home)` — pure global. The project override via loadProjectCompactionEngine(cwd) goes to cli.config.compactionEngine presumably, NOT saved. ✓ So carrying saved.compaction* can never leak a project pick.

FINAL: carry it. Update my bin comment accordingly (no null no-op args). Update agent_cli_config.dart's doc comment line "NEVER persisted by the host config save" — still TRUE (liveCompactionEngine is never persisted; saved.compactionEngine is the loaded global value). I'll leave agent_cli_config as-is — it says the LIVE override is never persisted, which remains true.

Hmm, hold on, let me re-read that comment once more: "NEVER persisted by the host config save: the session scope promises 'no file change', and the project/global scopes write their yaml through the targeted upsert themselves — the whole-file save keeps the on-disk `compaction:` block untouched instead."

"the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead" — with my change, the whole-file save RE-RENDERS compaction from the loaded value (untouched when identical after skip-when-unchanged... wait! With skip-when-unchanged: if saved.compaction == what's on disk (it IS — it was loaded from disk), the rendered compaction block may still differ from the raw block in FORMATTING (comments/spacing). So finalText != diskText → a write happens (formatting normalization) where old code kept the file untouched. The session-scope promise "no file change" — the session scope itself never calls persistConfig, so it holds.

I'll accept the typed render for compaction and fix the bin comment. Actually — you know what, let me keep this truly minimal-risk: the old code deliberately omitted compaction from the save object. The copyWith approach makes that IMPOSSIBLE without sentinel hacks. Between (a) sentinel-clearing hacks, (b) carrying compaction + updated comments, and (c) bin-side post-strip:

```dart
final persistShaped = saved.copyWith(...);
```

I choose (b) — carrying the loaded global compaction value is provably leak-free and value-faithful, and the emitter's render is strict-schema-complete. Update comments in bin to document why carrying `saved.compaction*` is safe (never the live pick). Also leave the on-disk comment in agent_cli_config.dart untouched (still accurate: the LIVE override is never persisted).

Hmm, wait. Let me re-check ONE more time whether there's a flow where `saved` is REBUILT from a live/mutated config... `saved` is `late final CliConfig` assigned once at line 238. persistConfig closure captures it. ✓ Never mutated.

And for correctness of the render round trip: `_compactionYaml` renders `compaction:\n  engine: structured\n` etc. fromYaml parses engine via CompactionEngine.fromSection and judgeBudgetSeconds via parseJudgeBudgetSeconds. Round trips. ✓

Now fix the bin edit: remove the two null no-op args and the misleading comment; replace with an accurate one.

The `compaction:` section is fully-typed and STRICT: only `engine` (classic|structured) and `judgeBudgetSeconds` parse — anything else throws at load. So a raw compaction block has exactly the two keys; the typed render is value-faithful. The only fidelity loss is intra-block comments.

Given the strictness, carrying saved.compaction is value-identical always. But the documented promise ("the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead") would become slightly untrue (comments).

Decision: honor the documented design EXACTLY — persistConfig must not carry compaction. To enable that cleanly with copyFrom-style semantics, I'll keep copyWith uniform BUT... hmm.

Actually — cleanest minimal solution: keep my copyWith null=keep AND simply have bin NOT pass the two `compactionEngine: null, compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds: null` args (they're no-ops), while making the copyWith base for compaction NOT saved... no.

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. What if the copyWith call passes overlays, and afterwards we let the BACKSTOP do its documented job for compaction by REMOVING the carried compaction from the emitted yaml? That's emitter logic, not caller logic — wrong layer.

Alternative: `_diskPreservedSections` re-attach only fires when omitted. What if `compaction` render... no, don't hack the emitter.

Let me reconsider: sentinel-clearing for ALL nullable section fields? That's the "proper" copyWith in many codebases: use a per-field sentinel wrapper. Too invasive.

PRAGMATIC FINAL DECISION: Give `copyWith` two extra OPTIONAL clearing parameters? No.

Honestly — re-examine the actual risk of carrying saved.compaction once more:
1. Settings-hub session scope: sets liveCompactionEngine; persistConfig NOT called by that flow (nothing else triggers) → no write → promise holds. Even if a later unrelated persistConfig happens in the same session: we persist saved.compaction (the global value loaded at boot) — NOT the session pick. No leak. ✓
2. Global scope: `_upsertConfigYaml(['compaction','engine'], ...)` writes the yaml surgically; liveCompactionEngine set. persistConfig never carries the LIVE value (it reads saved.*, loaded pre-session). Next boot loads the upserted file. ✓
3. Intra-block comments: lost on the next whole-file save that changes something. Minor, consistent with... hmm, actually NOT consistent: other raw-preserved blocks with NO renderer (memory, a2a, waiting) keep comments forever. Blocks WITH renders that are carried (redact, images, links, tools, cube, tui, trajectory, quota, agent...) lose intra-block comments on any content-changing save. compaction was the exception BECAUSE the flow deliberately avoided persisting it.

The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). With the leak concern gone, the remaining difference is only intra-block comment fidelity — and the emitter renders compaction only when non-default values exist.

The project override via loadProjectCompactionEngine(cwd) goes to cli.config.compactionEngine presumably, NOT saved. ✓ So carrying saved.compaction* can never leak a project pick.

The `compaction:` section is fully-typed and STRICT: only `engine` (classic|structured) and `judgeBudgetSeconds` parse — anything else throws at load. So a raw compaction block has exactly the two keys; the typed render is value-faithful. The only fidelity loss is intra-block comments.

Given the strictness, carrying saved.compaction is value-identical always. But the documented promise ("the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead") would become slightly untrue (comments).

Decision: honor the documented design EXACTLY — persistConfig must not carry compaction. To enable that cleanly with copyFrom-style semantics, I'll keep copyWith uniform BUT... hmm.

Actually — cleanest minimal solution: keep my copyWith null=keep AND simply have bin NOT pass the two `compactionEngine: null, compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds: null` args (they're no-ops), while making the copyWith base for compaction NOT saved... no.

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. What if the copyWith call passes overlays, and afterwards we let the BACKSTOP do its documented job for compaction by REMOVING the carried compaction from the emitted yaml? That's emitter logic, not caller logic — wrong layer.

Alternative: `_diskPreservedSections` re-attach only fires when omitted. What if `compaction` render... no, don't hack the emitter.

Let me reconsider: sentinel-clearing for ALL nullable section fields? That's the "proper" copyWith in many codebases: use a per-field sentinel wrapper. Too invasive.

PRAGMATIC FINAL DECISION: Give `copyWith` two extra OPTIONAL clearing parameters? No.

Honestly — re-examine the actual risk of carrying saved.compaction once more:
1. Settings-hub session scope: sets liveCompactionEngine; persistConfig NOT called by that flow (nothing else triggers) → no write → promise holds. Even if a later unrelated persistConfig happens in the same session: we persist saved.compaction (the global value loaded at boot) — NOT the session pick. No leak. ✓
2. Global scope: `_upsertConfigYaml(['compaction','engine'], ...)` writes the yaml surgically; liveCompactionEngine set. persistConfig never carries the LIVE value (it reads saved.*, loaded pre-session). Next boot loads the upserted file. ✓
3. Intra-block comments: lost on the next whole-file save that changes something. Minor, consistent with... hmm, actually NOT consistent: other raw-preserved blocks with NO renderer (memory, a2a, waiting) keep comments forever. Blocks WITH renders that are carried (redact, images, links, tools, cube, tui, trajectory, quota, agent...) lose intra-block comments on any content-changing save. compaction was the exception BECAUSE the flow deliberately avoided persisting it.

The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). With the leak concern gone, the remaining difference is only intra-block comment fidelity — and the emitter renders compaction only when non-default values exist.

Hmm, but wait — one more scenario to check: `boot resolved` value! Let me check how boot resolves the engine: is there a `--compaction` flag or project override that lands in `saved`? `saved = loadCliConfig(home)` — pure global. The project override via loadProjectCompactionEngine(cwd) goes to cli.config.compactionEngine presumably, NOT saved. ✓ So carrying saved.compaction* can never leak a project pick.

FINAL: carry it. Update my bin comment accordingly (no null no-op args). Update agent_cli_config.dart's doc comment line "NEVER persisted by the host config save" — still TRUE (liveCompactionEngine is never persisted; saved.compactionEngine is the loaded global value). I'll leave agent_cli_config as-is — it says the LIVE override is never persisted, which remains true.

"the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead" — with my change, the whole-file save RE-RENDERS compaction from the loaded value (untouched when identical after skip-when-unchanged... wait! With skip-when-unchanged: if saved.compaction == what's on disk (it IS — it was loaded from disk), the rendered compaction block may still differ from the raw block in FORMATTING (comments/spacing). So finalText != diskText → a write happens (formatting normalization) where old code kept the file untouched. The session-scope promise "no file change" — the session scope itself never calls persistConfig, so it holds.

I'll accept the typed render for compaction and fix the bin comment. Actually — you know what, let me keep this truly minimal-risk: the old code deliberately omitted compaction from the save object. The copyWith approach makes that IMPOSSIBLE without sentinel hacks. Between (a) sentinel-clearing hacks, (b) carrying compaction + updated comments, and (c) bin-side post-strip:

```

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). # Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per

  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

b203d3d gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang (#1509)
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

The CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with per-fix entries (e.g. "gh-1556: ..."). The previous bug fix commit b203d3d (gh-1507) touched CHANGELOG.md. So the convention: add a gh-1572 entry under `## Unreleased`. Let me check the gh-1507 entry format.

Given the strictness, carrying saved.compaction is value-identical always. But the documented promise ("the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead") would become slightly untrue (comments).

Decision: honor the documented design EXACTLY — persistConfig must not carry compaction. To enable that cleanly with copyFrom-style semantics, I'll keep copyWith uniform BUT... hmm.

Actually — cleanest minimal solution: keep my copyWith null=keep AND simply have bin NOT pass the two `compactionEngine: null, compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds: null` args (they're no-ops), while making the copyWith base for compaction NOT saved... no.

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. What if the copyWith call passes overlays, and afterwards we let the BACKSTOP do its documented job for compaction by REMOVING the carried compaction from the emitted yaml? That's emitter logic, not caller logic — wrong layer.

Alternative: `_diskPreservedSections` re-attach only fires when omitted. What if `compaction` render... no, don't hack the emitter.

Let me reconsider: sentinel-clearing for ALL nullable section fields? That's the "proper" copyWith in many codebases: use a per-field sentinel wrapper. Too invasive.

PRAGMATIC FINAL DECISION: Give `copyWith` two extra OPTIONAL clearing parameters? No.

Honestly — re-examine the actual risk of carrying saved.compaction once more:
1. Settings-hub session scope: sets liveCompactionEngine; persistConfig NOT called by that flow (nothing else triggers) → no write → promise holds. Even if a later unrelated persistConfig happens in the same session: we persist saved.compaction (the global value loaded at boot) — NOT the session pick. No leak. ✓
2. Global scope: `_upsertConfigYaml(['compaction','engine'], ...)` writes the yaml surgically; liveCompactionEngine set. persistConfig never carries the LIVE value (it reads saved.*, loaded pre-session). Next boot loads the upserted file. ✓
3. Intra-block comments: lost on the next whole-file save that changes something. Minor, consistent with... hmm, actually NOT consistent: other raw-preserved blocks with NO renderer (memory, a2a, waiting) keep comments forever. Blocks WITH renders that are carried (redact, images, links, tools, cube, tui, trajectory, quota, agent...) lose intra-block comments on any content-changing save. compaction was the exception BECAUSE the flow deliberately avoided persisting it.

The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). With the leak concern gone, the remaining difference is only intra-block comment fidelity — and the emitter renders compaction only when non-default values exist.

Hmm, but wait — one more scenario to check: `boot resolved` value! The project override via loadProjectCompactionEngine(cwd) goes to cli.config.compactionEngine presumably, NOT saved. ✓ So carrying saved.compaction* can never leak a project pick.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

b203d3d gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang (#1509)
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

The CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with per-fix entries (e.g. "gh-1556: ..."). The previous bug fix commit b203d3d (gh-1507) touched CHANGELOG.md. So the convention: add a gh-1572 entry under `## Unreleased`. Let me check the gh-1507 entry format.

blocks.text:
The `compaction:` section is fully-typed and STRICT: only `engine` (classic|structured) and `judgeBudgetSeconds` parse — anything else throws at load. So a raw compaction block has exactly the two keys; the typed render is value-faithful. The only fidelity loss is intra-block comments.

Given the strictness, carrying saved.compaction is value-identical always. But the documented promise ("the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead") would become slightly untrue (comments).

Decision: honor the documented design EXACTLY — persistConfig must not carry compaction. To enable that cleanly with copyFrom-style semantics, I'll keep copyWith uniform BUT... hmm.

Actually — cleanest minimal solution: keep my copyWith null=keep AND simply have bin NOT pass the two `compactionEngine: null, compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds: null` args (they're no-ops), while making the copyWith base for compaction NOT saved... no.

WAIT. Actually — much simpler idea. The persist-shaped config only needs `saved` as base. What if the copyWith call passes overlays, and afterwards we let the BACKSTOP do its documented job for compaction by REMOVING the carried compaction from the emitted yaml? That's emitter logic, not caller logic — wrong layer.

Alternative: `_diskPreservedSections` re-attach only fires when omitted. What if `compaction` render... no, don't hack the emitter.

Let me reconsider: sentinel-clearing for ALL nullable section fields? That's the "proper" copyWith in many codebases: use a per-field sentinel wrapper. Too invasive.

PRAGMATIC FINAL DECISION: Give `copyWith` two extra OPTIONAL clearing parameters? No.

Honestly — re-examine the actual risk of carrying saved.compaction once more:
1. Settings-hub session scope: sets liveCompactionEngine; persistConfig NOT called by that flow (nothing else triggers) → no write → promise holds. Even if a later unrelated persistConfig happens in the same session: we persist saved.compaction (the global value loaded at boot) — NOT the session pick. No leak. ✓
2. Global scope: `_upsertConfigYaml(['compaction','engine'], ...)` writes the yaml surgically; liveCompactionEngine set. persistConfig never carries the LIVE value (it reads saved.*, loaded pre-session). Next boot loads the upserted file. ✓
3. Intra-block comments: lost on the next whole-file save that changes something. Minor, consistent with... hmm, actually NOT consistent: other raw-preserved blocks with NO renderer (memory, a2a, waiting) keep comments forever. Blocks WITH renders that are carried (redact, images, links, tools, cube, tui, trajectory, quota, agent...) lose intra-block comments on any content-changing save. compaction was the exception BECAUSE the flow deliberately avoided persisting it.

The exception existed because of the LEAK concern (live override), which my copyWith approach doesn't have (it carries saved., never live). With the leak concern gone, the remaining difference is only intra-block comment fidelity — and the emitter renders compaction only when non-default values exist.

Hmm, but wait — one more scenario to check: `boot resolved` value! Let me check how boot resolves the engine: is there a `--compaction` flag or project override that lands in `saved`? `saved = loadCliConfig(home)` — pure global. The project override via loadProjectCompactionEngine(cwd) goes to cli.config.compactionEngine presumably, NOT saved. ✓ So carrying saved.compaction* can never leak a project pick.

FINAL: carry it. Update my bin comment accordingly (no null no-op args). Update agent_cli_config.dart's doc comment line "NEVER persisted by the host config save" — still TRUE (liveCompactionEngine is never persisted; saved.compactionEngine is the loaded global value). I'll leave agent_cli_config as-is — it says the LIVE override is never persisted, which remains true.

Hmm, hold on, let me re-read that comment once more: "NEVER persisted by the host config save: the session scope promises 'no file change', and the project/global scopes write their yaml through the targeted upsert themselves — the whole-file save keeps the on-disk `compaction:` block untouched instead."

"the whole-file save keeps the on-disk compaction: block untouched instead" — with my change, the whole-file save RE-RENDERS compaction from the loaded value (untouched when identical after skip-when-unchanged... wait! With skip-when-unchanged: if saved.compaction == what's on disk (it IS — it was loaded from disk), the rendered compaction block may still differ from the raw block in FORMATTING (comments/spacing). So finalText != diskText → a write happens (formatting normalization) where old code kept the file untouched. The session-scope promise "no file change" — the session scope itself never calls persistConfig, so it holds.

I'll accept the typed render for compaction and fix the bin comment. Actually — you know what, let me keep this truly minimal-risk: the old code deliberately omitted compaction from the save object. The copyWith approach makes that IMPOSSIBLE without sentinel hacks. Between (a) sentinel-clearing hacks, (b) carrying compaction + updated comments, and (c) bin-side post-strip:

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

- fix(cli): gh-1572 — `fa` boot no longer rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml`
  from a lossy config. `persistConfig` (bin/fah_runapp.dart) built a
  fresh `CliConfig` carrying only some fields and `persistConfig()` ran
  unconditionally at boot, so every launch silently dropped the user's
  `spills:`, `subagents:`, `jobs:`, `headless:`, `agent:`, `quota:`,
  `tui:`, `trajectory:`, `waiting:`, `power.hold` and `auto_update`
  settings (first reported on 1.0.547). Three cooperating fixes: the
  boot save is now `saved.copyWith(<live overlays>)` so every parsed
  section rides along by construction; `CliConfig.copyWith` replaces the
  drifted hand-rolled `withCustomProviders` field list (itself dropping
  spills/subagents/waiting/jobs/agentMode/misuseBreaker/streamThinking
  inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge step); the `_diskPreservedSections`
  disk backstop covers every known top-level key. `spills:` renders in
  `toYaml` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml`) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`
  persists too; an unchanged save no longer rewrites the file at all.

b203d3d gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang (#1509)
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: see CI — local run green (no regressions).

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

## 1.0.508

- fix(cli): gh-1459 — headless `fa -p` no longer orphans live background
  shell jobs. `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` drained only in-flight
  subagent jobs, so a run whose model was still waiting on a
  `bash background:true` command (gh-1440's full test suite) printed the
  detach summary and exited, killing the job with the container — the
  result it was explicitly waiting for never reached anyone. Live shell
  jobs now drain exactly like subagents: the settles ride the existing
  `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn path (steered into reaction runs the
  drain awaits, loop capped at 10 rounds), suppressed jobs
  (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not
  awaited, and a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction
  run awaited before exit. BOTH loops share ONE wall-clock ceiling, the
  new `headless:` config section (`shellJobDrainMs`, default 30 min,
  strict parse; `0` restores the detach-immediately behavior) — a
  never-settling watch-loop detaches with an observable
  `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line instead of hanging headless,
